source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Inattention for 8 months at school, with no similar symptoms at home or in other settings.","B":"Inattention or hyperactivity for 8 months at home and school, with clear impairment in daily functioning.","C":"Inattention for 6 weeks at home and school after a major family disruption, with declining grades.","D":"Inattention for 8 months at home and school, with age-appropriate functioning and no meaningful impairment."}}
source_row.rationale: ADHD evaluation is supported by a persistent pattern lasting at least 6 months, occurring in at least two settings, and causing functional impairment. Option B includes all three features. A is limited to one setting, C is too brief and has an alternative contextual explanation, and D lacks impairment.
source_row.source_detail: CDC ADHD diagnostic criteria section: symptoms persist at least 6 months, are present in two or more settings, interfere with or reduce quality of social/school/work functioning, and are not better explained by another disorder. CDC Clinical Care of ADHD in Children dated 2026-07-30; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity: mental-health symptom recognition, therapeutic communication, professional boundaries, coping and psychosocial support as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
